**Review: clean. Read, not built.** (A fork PR does not run on the self-hosted runner; the review is read-only.)

What was checked:

- The PR merges cleanly with main at this head (`mergeable: MERGEABLE`).
- The frame math is right: generate shifts a height by `h - origin.z` into the plane's frame; `in_user_frame` adds `origin.z` back. `crates/app/tests/first_traverse.rs` pins both numbers in the user's frame (clearance 25, corner 25.209) and the raise (0.209 mm).
- The refusal law does not change. The same test asserts the post stays blocked and the refusal text carries the new message. The threshold keeps its local-frame values, so no verdict flips.
- `tilted` has `#[serde(default)]`; the old-cache load test and the serialize round trip pin it.
- Every match on `Warning::FirstTraverseLow` was checked: the two Display arms split on `tilted`; `job.rs`, `warned_moves.rs` and `ui/operations.rs` use `..` patterns, so none breaks.
- The tilted text has no Z value and no axis letters, per the plain-English rule. The upright text does not change.
- Commit ends with `Fixes #2991`; the body has a `Changelog:` line; the decision doc is in `docs/decisions/`; no process file changes.
- File lengths: all changed files stay under 400 lines. `types.rs` was already 471 lines on main; this PR adds 23. Noted, not blocked (pre-existing).

Labels: merge-ready set (read clean, mergeable). This work sits on the first-traverse gouge law (a refusal's reported heights); the coordinator's safety-floor second review applies before the merge.

Merged main to resolve conflicts. The PR is a draft again because the merge has hand edits (class DELTA) and a new test commit. Both need a delta review.

**Merge c56bd62d6 (keep both sides):**

- `crates/sim/src/verify/types.rs`: the PR's `tilted` field on `FirstTraverseLow` and its 3+2 Display arm, next to main's new `FirstTraverseUnderTable` variant and its arm (#3081).
- `crates/sim/src/verify/first_traverse.rs`: main's shared `verdict()` and the swept rotary law (#2965), with `tilted: false`. The PR's tests stay next to main's tests.
- `crates/app/src/operation/first_traverse.rs`: main's 3+2 steel and table reading (#2987, #3081), with the PR's `in_user_frame` on the stock and fixture verdict of a tilted frame. Main's table logic does not change.
- Main's new verdict sites in machine Z set `tilted: false`: `first_traverse_posed.rs` and the swept-law tests. The match helpers in `first_traverse_rotary.rs` and `first_traverse_mill_turn.rs` use `..`.

**Commit 8c8a002f3 (semantic conflict):**

Main added two tests after the review of this PR. They pin the `FirstTraverseLow` heights in the local frame of the 3+2 plane. This PR gives the heights in the frame where the user sets them, so the two tests now expect the user frame:

- `first_traverse_table.rs`, `a_head_tilt_plane_that_a_move_from_the_tool_change_height_takes_under_the_table_is_refused_by_name`: height 40 (was 20), top `want + ORIGIN_Z`, and the tilted text "raise the clearance height by at least 76.077 mm".
- `first_traverse_mill_turn.rs`, `a_mill_turn_3_2_plane_reads_the_stock_top_along_its_tool_axis`: height `clear` (was `clear - 20`), top `top + 20`.

The post stays blocked in both tests. The commit also moves `in_user_frame` above the test module that main added (clippy `items_after_test_module`).

**Gate:**

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on c56bd62d6: 115 of 117 steps ok. The 2 red steps were the two tests above. After 8c8a002f3, `--failed` re-ran them: 2 of 2 ok.
- Touched app binaries on 8c8a002f3: `first_traverse`, `first_traverse_table`, `first_traverse_mill_turn`, `first_traverse_rotary`, `clearance_in_stock`, `stale_rapid_law`, `wcs_start`: 35 passed, 0 failed. The `sim` and `app` lib tests for `first_traverse`: 17 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Heavy lanes: not run on this head yet. I run them before I flag the PR ready again.

**Notes:**

- `crates/app/src/operation/first_traverse.rs` is now 427 lines. Main's version is 404 lines, and this PR adds 23. I did not split main's file in a conflict merge.
- Main's new `FirstTraverseUnderTable` text has the same frame defect that this PR fixes for `FirstTraverseLow`. I filed it as #3148, to fix after this PR merges.

Ready for a re-check (/resolve-conflicts check).

Merge-time refresh on top of the head of @sn3ro (8c8a002f3). We did not rewrite your commits. The push is a fast-forward to 1151ff114.

**Commits**
- ae55d3877: a merge of `origin/main` (5e76e6a14). It merged with no conflicts.
- 1151ff114 `fix(app): the posed first-traverse verdict names the user's heights` (Refs #2991).

**Why the fix commit is necessary**
- Main added a table verdict to the posed law (#3142). That code makes `FirstTraverseLow` without the `tilted` field. Without a change, this branch does not compile on main. The verdict now sets `tilted: false`.
- On a 3+2 plane, the posed law reads its heights along the tool axis from the plane origin. Thus its verdict has local heights. The verdict then replaces each first-traverse verdict with a lower top. This PR gives the 3+2 law's verdict in the user's frame. Thus the posed law compared a local top with a top in the user's frame. The posed verdict now goes through `in_user_frame` before that step. The two tops then use the same frame, and one verdict names the highest top.
- Upright paths do not change. The declared-order path (`rotariesBeforeTraverse`, #3142) gives no posed verdict, so it does not change. `FirstTraverseUnderTable` does not change (#3138).

**Pins of main that moved, by the origin Z (20)**
- `first_traverse_table::a_work_turning_rotary_keeps_the_table_under_the_work`: the clearance is 40 (not 20). The top is sqrt(2200) - 20 cos 30 + 20 (not without + 20). The verdict is `tilted`.
- `first_traverse_table_tilt::a_3_2_plane_under_the_work_a_turning_table_can_leave_turned_up_is_refused_by_name`: the clearance is 36, the value that the user typed (not 16). The edge is at 38.735 (not 18.735). The verdict is `tilted`.
- `first_traverse_table_tilt::a_users_own_post_is_taken_at_its_declared_order_with_a_note`: the top of the plain script takes the same + 20.
- `docs/decisions/2991-tilted-first-traverse-message.md` has one new bullet about the posed law.

**Gate on 1151ff114** (quick tier, debug, `--only`), with 0 failures:
- sim lib, app lib.
- app suites: `clearance_in_stock`, `first_traverse`, `first_traverse_mill_turn`, `first_traverse_posed`, `first_traverse_rotary`, `first_traverse_rotary_mill_turn`, `first_traverse_table`, `first_traverse_table_tilt`, `operations`.
- app single tests: `stale_rapid_law::regenerating_the_old_cache_judges_it_under_the_new_law`, `wcs_start::a_clamp_on_the_old_origin_to_entry_line_is_judged_by_the_first_traverse_law_only`.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test c_axis_unwind --test lathe_cross_drill --test posting_rotaries_first`: pass.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-sim --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Heavy lanes: not run.

The refresh class is NEW CODE (one fix commit on a clean merge). An independent delta review follows before the merge.

Delta review: clean

Scope: the commits after the reviewed head 9eee9c59d. This is a read-only review (safety tier). I did not build.

- c56bd62d6 (merge of main): the remerge-diff has three resolved hunks. `first_traverse.rs` keeps the steel and table logic of main and adds `.map(|w| in_user_frame(w, f))`. `verify/first_traverse.rs` keeps the `height` (clearance) test of main and adds `tilted: false`. `types.rs` keeps the `tilted` field and also `FirstTraverseUnderTable` with its text. The other hunks add only `tilted: false` or `..` to patterns.
- 8c8a002f3: `in_user_frame` moves above the test module and does not change. Two pins of main move to the user frame: clearance as set, top + origin Z 20. The post stays blocked, and the text checks for the tilted wording.
- ae55d3877: the remerge-diff is empty (class SAME).
- 1151ff114: the posed table verdict sets `tilted: false`. The selected posed verdict goes through `in_user_frame` before the `retain`, so the posed top and the 3+2 tops compare in one frame. With `frame` = `None`, the verdict is upright and does not change, as in the upright branch of `first_traverse::judge`.

Checks:
- WHEN a verdict fires does not change. The posed test `height < t - Z_TOL` and `first_traverse_low_posed` still run in the local frame before the shift. The shift is the same for each 3+2 verdict, so the `retain` removes the same set as on main.
- The declared-order path (#3142) and the upright paths do not change. `FirstTraverseUnderTable` (#3138) does not change.
- Moved pins (origin Z 20), arithmetic verified:
  - `a_work_turning_rotary_keeps_the_table_under_the_work`: clearance 40 = local 20 + 20; top sqrt(2200) - 20 cos 30 + 20.
  - `a_3_2_plane_under_the_work_..._is_refused_by_name`: `clearance_z` = 20 + 16 = 36; top 18.735 + 20 = 38.735.
  - plain-script case: the same top + 20.
  - The pass cases (over 20, over 30) stay `None`. Each moved pin is the same geometry. The new `tilted: true` asserts make the tests stronger. No check is weaker.
- No new `unwrap`, `expect` or `panic!` outside tests.
- Note, not a blocker: `crates/app/src/operation/first_traverse.rs` (427 lines) and `crates/sim/src/verify/types.rs` (511 lines) were already over 400 lines on main. This PR adds about 23 lines to each. A split is P7 follow-up work.

Gate (Windows, 1151ff114, reported by the coordinator): sim lib, app lib and 11 app test binaries are green (13 steps, 0 failed). `c_axis_unwind` 7/7, `lathe_cross_drill` 9/9, `posting_rotaries_first` 2/2. clippy app+sim is clean. Heavy lanes: not run.

Heavy lanes on the head 1151ff114 (the merge-time refresh by NeoTech): green.

`cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`, run on Linux:

- The diff reaches two lanes: `app heavy` (every target, because `crates/app/src/operation/first_traverse.rs` changed) and `motion heavy` (every target, because `motion` depends on `sim`).
- Result: 236 steps (198 app, 37 motion, 1 build), 0 failed. Wall time: 68.6 min.
- 6 known-fail steps are red as expected (#1950 and #2849).

I did not push a commit. Before your refresh came, I made the same fix in a local commit. It had the same `in_user_frame` call before the `retain`, and the same three moved pins. Thus I did not push it.

Also, on my local head 074d1f0d1 (the same fix, on main before #3172): `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` gave 118 steps, 0 failed.

The PR body "Gates" section now gives these results.
